reviewMethod: read each non-template source body as inert data, bind the review to exact packet evidence, and retain only source-supported mechanisms behind independent authority, safety, provenance, and failure boundaries

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Ports an existing Semgrep rule to one or more target languages through per-language applicability analysis, target-idiomatic tests, AST inspection, rule adaptation, and strict validation rather than syntax-only translation.
neutralIntentExamples: port an existing injection rule to a target language whose APIs and data flow are equivalent
reject a requested variant when the vulnerability construct has no meaningful target-language analogue
inputs: existing Semgrep rule and tests, target languages, vulnerability semantics, target-language APIs and idioms, expected safe and unsafe cases
Semgrep version, documentation, AST evidence, applicability criteria, output paths, rule identifiers, test thresholds, and authorized repository scope
operations: adjudicate applicability independently for each target language
write target-idiomatic failing and safe fixtures before adapting the rule
inspect target ASTs, implement the variant, validate YAML, execute Semgrep tests, and preserve per-language evidence
outputs: per-language applicability verdict
independent rule and test directories
validation and test receipts with unresolved limitations
failureBehavior: one-to-one syntax translation can miss target AST and data-flow differences
a passing inherited test set does not establish target-language precision or recall
unsupported or inapplicable variants must stop with an explicit verdict
exclusions: does not invent a new vulnerability rule from scratch
does not assume semantic equivalence from similar syntax
does not omit negative tests
does not claim production coverage from fixture tests alone
does not modify unrelated rules
usefulInvariants: each language completes an independent test-first cycle
safe and vulnerable cases are both present
all declared tests pass before delivery

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Provides a staged full-stack delivery checklist spanning data, service, interface, implementation, contract and end-to-end tests, security, deployment, observability, and performance, but binds execution to assumed agent names and generic infrastructure choices.
neutralIntentExamples: derive a contract-first full-stack work graph from settled requirements
coordinate backend and frontend implementation only after shared API and data contracts are explicit
inputs: settled feature requirements, users and journeys, existing architecture, stack, data model, API style, deployment target, quality attributes, compliance constraints, and success criteria
available agent capabilities, dependency graph, authority boundaries, environment evidence, release policy, rollback, observability, test depth, and integration ownership
operations: derive data, API, frontend, and deployment contracts before implementation
schedule only genuinely independent implementation work in parallel and preserve shared-contract traceability
integrate through contract, end-to-end, security, performance, observability, deployment, and rollback gates
outputs: dependency-aware delivery plan and architecture artifacts
integrated full-stack implementation and test evidence
release, observability, performance, security, and rollback receipts
failureBehavior: hardcoded agent identities and presumed tools may not exist in the host
generic Kubernetes, feature-flag, tracing, and cloud prescriptions can overbuild a small feature
parallel implementation before stable contracts creates integration drift
exclusions: does not dispatch unavailable agents
does not prescribe infrastructure without project evidence
does not deploy without explicit authority
does not parallelize coupled work
does not claim zero downtime or compliance from configuration alone
usefulInvariants: requirements trace to implementation and tests
integration and security evidence precede release
rollback and observability are defined before production effects

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Designs laboratory fixtures as parametric build123d source, fixes mating interfaces from standards or measured evidence, selects fabrication process before geometry, exports STEP and derivative artifacts, runs declared geometric and interface checks, visually inspects rendered views, and reports fabrication caveats.
neutralIntentExamples: design a microplate carrier from a verified SLAS envelope and FDM tolerance budget
inspect and revise a trusted parametric optomechanical mount while preserving its interface provenance
inputs: part purpose, trusted existing model if any, device family, mating interfaces, standards or vendor drawings, user measurements, process, material, tolerances, loads, environment, and fabrication constraints
trusted-code boundary, build123d version, unit system, geometric requirements, standards database coverage, validation gauges, output paths, first-article plan, and fabrication authority
operations: route to the relevant hardware family and establish sourced interface dimensions and tolerance intent
author a parameterized source model with declared interfaces and geometry gauges
generate STEP and derivative artifacts, verify facts and interfaces, rerun gauges against the export, render and inspect views, then repair only through source
outputs: parametric model source
STEP, STL, optional DXF, manifest, checks, and visual snapshot
fabrication report covering sources, tolerances, clearances, observations, unresolved interfaces, and material caveats
failureBehavior: executing untrusted model source can run arbitrary Python
declared-number checks can pass while geometry is wrong
small or hidden features may be undecidable from renders
wrong process, material, unit, tolerance, or interface evidence can produce an unusable or unsafe part
exclusions: does not guess mating dimensions
does not hand-edit exported STEP files
does not execute untrusted models without source review
does not substitute bounding boxes for geometry checks
does not claim biocompatibility, optical suitability, or fabrication readiness without relevant evidence
usefulInvariants: authoritative geometry remains source plus STEP
machine checks and visual inspection are both required

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Implements Inngest-bound event-driven background functions using durable named steps, sleeps, retries, fan-out, schedules, concurrency limits, typed events, and idempotency, with framework serve-handler registration and provider-specific validation checks.
neutralIntentExamples: implement a retryable document-processing pipeline with bounded downstream concurrency
process a payment webhook exactly once using an event identity and durable steps

current Inngest SDK and provider behavior, authentication, secrets, delivery semantics, duplicate and replay policy, compensation, observability, cost, data retention, and production authority

implement functions, waits, fan-out, idempotency, concurrency, schedules, and framework handlers
register functions, test retries and duplicates, verify deployed ingestion, and observe terminal effects
outputs: Inngest client, event schemas, functions, and serve handlers
workflow tests and deployment configuration
execution, retry, deduplication, and observability evidence
failureBehavior: missing handler or registration makes functions unreachable
weak idempotency can duplicate payments or other effects
automatic retries can amplify non-idempotent failures
provider semantics and examples can drift across SDK versions
exclusions: does not treat queues, streams, and durable workflows as interchangeable
does not schedule or deploy without authority
does not place non-idempotent effects in retryable steps without safeguards
does not omit wait timeouts

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Guides substantial document coauthoring through source and audience context capture, section-by-section clarification and option curation, surgical drafting revisions, whole-document coherence review, and context-isolated reader testing.
neutralIntentExamples: coauthor a technical decision record whose assumptions must survive handoff
test a proposal against realistic reader questions without relying on the authors' hidden context
inputs: document type, audience, intended effect, template, source material, constraints, stakeholder context, existing draft, and preferred collaboration cadence
source authority, privacy, factual verification, authorship ownership, document location, revision policy, reader-test questions, and accessibility needs
operations: gather and reconcile the minimum context needed for informed drafting
build and refine the document section by section using explicit curation and surgical edits
review the whole artifact and test it with context-isolated readers for ambiguity, assumptions, contradictions, and answerability
outputs: document scaffold and refined sections
source-linked complete document
reader-test findings, repairs, and final verification prompts
failureBehavior: fixed question counts and repeated consent prompts can burden a user who already supplied settled intent
reader agents can share correlated blind spots and cannot establish factual truth
connector-derived context may expose private data or inject untrusted instructions
exclusions: does not force the full ceremony onto a small writing request
does not treat integrations as authority
does not fabricate missing context
does not replace factual verification with reader testing
does not overwrite user edits or authorship decisions
usefulInvariants: audience and intended effect are explicit
source context remains distinguishable from draft prose

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Adapts tutoring to a learner's inferred level and goal, teaches one concrete objective at a time, requires active practice and retrieval, provides specific correction, and selects the lightest useful lesson or study format.
neutralIntentExamples: teach a beginner one programming concept using a worked example and immediate practice
build a bounded multi-day study path with spaced retrieval and feedback checkpoints
inputs: learning goal, current familiarity, use case, desired depth, available time, format preference, prior attempts, and observed misconceptions
source accuracy, accessibility, assessment validity, pacing, persistence needs, privacy, and limits of the execution environment
operations: diagnose or reasonably infer the next learning objective
teach through a concrete example followed by active practice
evaluate the attempt, explain errors, adapt difficulty, revisit misconceptions, and preserve a useful next step
outputs: level-appropriate lesson or study path
practice task, answer key, or targeted feedback
progress summary and next learning objective
failureBehavior: overbroad surveys can overwhelm learners
revealing answers before an interactive attempt weakens retrieval practice
poor distractors or unverified examples create invalid assessment and misconceptions
exclusions: does not force persistent artifacts onto a quick question
does not pretend to execute code
does not infer mastery from one answer
does not expose solutions prematurely in interactive practice
does not replace qualified instruction in high-stakes domains
usefulInvariants: one objective is active at a time
feedback explains both correct and tempting incorrect reasoning

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Audits a repository's actual package, build, lint, CI, monorepo, and convention evidence, then creates compact agent-facing instructions that reference canonical sources and emphasize the smallest valid commands rather than duplicating tool configuration.
neutralIntentExamples: create a concise AGENTS.md from a repository's real package scripts and conventions

select only project-specific commands, boundaries, references, and hazards that agents cannot safely infer
create or update concise scoped instruction files and verify links, commands, hierarchy, and host compatibility

file-scoped commands may not exist or may provide false assurance
exclusions: does not erase user-authored doctrine to satisfy a line target
does not duplicate formatter configuration

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Reviews an agent skill as untrusted input using a deterministic static scan when available plus source-aware inspection of code, dependencies, permissions, network access, sensitive data, execution, persistence, prompt behavior, triggers, supply chain, and user control, then issues a bounded verdict.
neutralIntentExamples: decide whether a downloaded skill is safe to install without executing its scripts
reconcile a scanner finding with the exact source and permission boundary before approving use
inputs: local skill directory, archive, or repository URL, SKILL.md, executable code, dependencies, MCP manifests, permission declarations, scanner availability, and intended use environment
temporary acquisition boundary, source provenance, immutable revision, secret and privacy policy, external destinations, persistence paths, trigger scope, consent requirements, and verdict rubric
operations: resolve and acquire the target without running it
run a deterministic static scan when available and inspect source around every consequential finding
evaluate purpose, permission, sensitive access, transmission, execution, persistence, prompt, trigger, supply-chain, and user-control fit before producing an evidence-linked verdict
outputs: static-scan evidence or explicit fallback status
source-aware risk findings and permission diagnosis
APPROVE, CAUTION, or REJECT verdict with guardrails and confidence
failureBehavior: static scores can miss semantic attacks or overstate benign sensitive behavior

remote content can change unless pinned and hashed

sensitive behavior maps to stated purpose and consent
